## Why visit

A particularly useful meal anchor for this trip, combining Indian vegetarian food with beer made in the same room. The tanks beneath the glass atrium make the production side visible while communal tables encourage a relaxed tasting-and-sharing meal. Its cask lines and CAMRA-listed real cider give it more relevance to your brief than a generic craft-beer restaurant. Choose this Manchester branch when the brewery experience matters: it adds a different setting to a day of old pubs and a substantial food break without abandoning the beer hunt.

## Beer

The operator advertises two cask and sixteen keg lines, mixing Bundobust beers with collaborations and guests. Beer is produced on site; individual taps change.

## Cider and perry

**Real cider documented; reconfirm stock.** CAMRA explicitly flags real cider and names Hogan’s. Check the current product and availability when ordering; the listing is not a live stock list.

See [how cider is classified](../real-cider.md).

## Food

Indian vegetarian and vegan street-food dishes designed for sharing. The operator advertises its full food menu daily; reserve for a planned meal.

## Plan the visit

Select the Oxford Street Brewery when booking: Manchester Piccadilly is a separate Bundobust. The official postcode is used here; CAMRA gives a different postcode for the same street address. Kitchen and bar closing times differ.

**Getting there:** Near Manchester Oxford Road railway station and St Peter’s Square Metrolink; useful alongside the southern city-centre pubs.

Check [November transport issues](../logistics.md) for date-specific disruption.
